correctness.rationale: The automorphism average reduces the SLEM value (not unrestricted uniqueness) to shell kernels; Walsh eigenvalues are quadratic Krawtchouk expressions. Degree-one and parity eigenvalue bounds force shell masses (0,2/(d+1),(d-1)/(d+1)) for d>=4. The d=3 interpolation identity gives 1/7 and fixes every radial eigenvalue; full saturation of nonconstant Walsh modes at d=3 and d=4 forces each unaveraged optimizer to coincide with the radial kernel by Rayleigh equality. At d>=5 degree-one and parity mode saturation forces each vertex holding mass zero, bit-flip marginal 2/(d+1), and total one-bit mass 2/(d+1); strict slack of interior modes allows the displayed 4-direction translation-invariant perturbation. Pair-weight constraints leave binom(d,2)-1 coordinates, with an open feasible neighborhood. I independently checked rational Walsh eigenvalues and the perturbation for d=2..10, not as proof of all d.

value.rationale: This is not merely the known fastest-mixing optimum: it gives a sharp uniqueness-to-flexibility transition at d=5, necessary rowwise constraints for all optimal noninvariant chains, and a precise local dimension of alternative optimal reversible implementations, useful in secondary-cost fast-mixing designs.

final_claim: For symmetric stochastic matrices on the Boolean d-cube with transitions at Hamming distance <=2, the SLEM optimum is 0 (d=2), 1/7 (d=3), and (d-3)/(d+1) (d>=4); the unrestricted optimizer is unique iff 2<=d<=4; for d>=5 every optimizer has zero holding and fixed one-bit and per-bit flip masses 2/(d+1), while the translation-invariant optimal face has local affine dimension binom(d,2)-1.
limitations: Graph support Hamming <=2, symmetric stochastic real P only; translation-invariant local face dimension does not equal full unrestricted optimal face dimension.
Existing edge-transitive theory already covers the optimum value.

Any previously unindexed exact classification of equality cases for halved-hypercube fastest-mixing chains is a possible priority overlap.
